prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1318; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported being struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant, who described the collision and the pain felt in the neck and lower back immediately after. The account matched the first-notice report in every detail.

Entry 3: Responding officer's report obtained. It places the claimant in the passenger seat of the vehicle at the time of impact and records the other driver's account of the left turn.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement reviewed. Both describe the collision the same way as the claimant, and two independent witnesses have confirmed the sequence of events.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspected and the damage to the front quarter panel and bumper is consistent with the impact described. No prior damage to the vehicle appears in the file or in the records checked.

Entry 6: Policy confirmed in force at the time of loss, and the driver is listed as a named insured. Nothing in the underwriting history points to damage predating the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Medical records received. The neck and back strain diagnosis fits the type and force of the crash, and no earlier treatment to either area is on record with the providers or prior carriers checked.

Entry 8: Treatment billing has risen to many times the typical course for this kind of strain, with near-daily visits. Several weeks after the accident, the claimant reported pain in an additional body area not mentioned at first.

Entry 9: Claimant has given the same account in each conversation so far. Medical review is requested to confirm the treatment plan against accepted guidelines before the file is evaluated further.
